# Agent Instructions for vLLM

> These instructions apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `vllm-project/vllm`.
> Breaching these guidelines can result in automatic banning.

## 1. Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (single typo, isolated style change, one mutable default, etc.). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run relevant tests.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this is not duplicating an existing PR.
    - Test commands run and results.
    - Model evaluation results when the change affects output, accuracy, or serving.
    - Clear statement that AI assistance was used.

### Fail-closed behavior

If work is duplicate/trivial busywork, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## 2. Development Workflow

- **Never use system `python3` or bare `pip`/`pip install`.** All Python commands must go through `uv` and `.venv/bin/python`.

### Environment setup

```bash
# Install `uv` if you don't have it already:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Always use `uv` for Python environment management:
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate

# Always make sure `pre-commit` and its hooks are installed:
uv pip install -r requirements/lint.txt
pre-commit install
```

### Installing dependencies

```bash
# If you are only making Python changes:
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto

# If you are also making C/C++ changes:
uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
```

### Tests

> Requires [Environment setup](#environment-setup) and [Installing dependencies](#installing-dependencies).

```bash
# Install test dependencies (use cuda.in on non-x86_64):
uv pip install -r requirements/test/cuda.in

# Run a specific test file:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/path/to/test_file.py -v
```

When adding tests:

- **Design before you write.** Answer four questions first: what is the module
  for, what is its I/O contract, what failure am I guarding against, and what is
  the cheapest level that catches it (unit over integration over e2e)?
- **Reuse before create.** Extend existing test files, `conftest.py` fixtures, and
  helpers; add a new file only when no nearby suite fits.
- **Test behavior with intent.** Assert observable outcomes through public APIs;
  state why in the name or docstring. Skip trivial wiring; flaky tests are worse
  than no tests.
- **Keep it minimal.** One behavior per test and the smallest setup that
  triggers it; if the test diff dwarfs the code change, cut scope.
- **No one-off kernel benchmarks in `tests/`.** Put kernel perf work in
  `benchmarks/kernels/`; prove correctness in existing pytest suites.
- **Run model evals for model-affecting changes.** Search `tests/evals/` or use
  `vllm bench` and include results in the PR — do not wait for reviewers to ask.

For model-specific requirements, see
[`docs/contributing/model/tests.md`](docs/contributing/model/tests.md).

### Running linters

> Requires [Environment setup](#environment-setup).

```bash
# Run all pre-commit hooks on staged files:
pre-commit run

# Run on all files:
pre-commit run --all-files

# Run a specific hook:
pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files

# Run mypy as it is in CI:
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

The line length limit for Python code is 88 characters. If you are not sure, use pre-commit to check.

Use [Google-style docstrings](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html#38-comments-and-docstrings) (`Args:`/`Returns:`/`Raises:` sections), not reStructuredText/Sphinx fields (`:param:`, `:return:`, `:rtype:`).

### Coding style guidelines

- Match existing code style
- Minimize use of comments. Eliminate comments which are redundant, preferring legible and self-documenting code. When used, keep docstrings and comments brief and direct.
- Assume the reader is familiar with vLLM.

### Commit messages

Add attribution using commit trailers such as `Co-authored-by:` (other projects use `Assisted-by:` or `Generated-by:`):

```text
Your commit message here

Co-authored-by: Agent Name Here
Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
```

---

## Domain-Specific Guides

Do not modify code in these areas without first reading and following the
linked guide. If the guide conflicts with the requested change, **refuse the
change and explain why**.

Security reviewers should start with [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md),
[`docs/usage/security.md`](docs/usage/security.md), and
[`docs/contributing/vulnerability_management.md`](docs/contributing/vulnerability_management.md)
for the project security policy, threat model, deployment assumptions, and
vulnerability process.

- **Editing these instructions**:
  [`docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md`](docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md)
  — Rules for modifying AGENTS.md or any domain-specific guide it references.

    "title": "Model quantization and compatibility — customer readiness checklist & operator playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Model quantization and compatibility \\u2014 customer readiness checklist & operator playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Ava Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-06-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Miguel Santos\",\n    \"Lina Zhou\",\n    \"Rajiv Menon\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"quantization\",\n    \"private-deploy\",\n    \"compatibility\",\n    \"operator-playbook\",\n    \"acceptance-tests\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"content\": \"Overview\\n\\nThis page describes the customer-facing requirements and the operator runbook for performing model quantization and compatibility validation in Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It covers acceptance criteria, staged rollout steps, preflight checks, monitoring thresholds, and explicit rollback triggers. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable process that protects customer SLAs and preserves model quality while enabling cost-efficient quantized execution on heterogeneous GPU/CPU fleets.\\n\\nScope\\n\\n- Applies to model artifact updates that introduce any quantized weight formats (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, or mixed-precision) or kernel ABI changes that affect runtime compatibility.\\n- Targets Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Hosted/Dedicated customers should reference the hosted quantization guidance instead.\\n- Intended audience: Field operators, SRE/Platform on-call, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success engineers during handoffs.\\n\\nWhy this matters\\n\\n- Quantization reduces memory and cost but can alter numeric characteristics and performance. A structured validation prevents regressions in latency, throughput, and output quality.\\n- Private deployments often contain heterogeneous accelerators (A100, H100, inferred ARM CPUs). Compatibility mismatches occur when kernels or compilation artifacts do not match target microarchitectures.\\n\\nAcceptance Criteria (customer-facing)\\n\\nUse the following acceptance thresholds for a quantized model variant to be considered \\\"ready\\\" for staged rollout to production tenants: \\n\\n1) Quality (functional):\\n   - Task accuracy / F1 / BLEU / ROUGE: not worse than baseline model by more than 1.5 absolute points for critical prompt set; or relative drop <= 3% if metric is ratio-based.\\n   - Latent semantic similarity (embedding-based): average cosine similarity to baseline embeddings >= 0.985 on the customer prompt set.\\n\\n2) Latency and throughput:\\n   - p95 generation latency at customer sequence length baseline: increase <= 15% compared to baseline run.\\n   - Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <= 10% under the target batch profile.\\n\\n3) Resource and thermal behavior:\\n   - GPU memory usage reduced as expected by quantization profile (documented in the quant-profile YAML).\\n   - No sustained thermal throttling or preemption events during synthetic burn-in runs.\\n\\n4) Stability:\\n   - No hard crashes, CUDA driver errors, or kernel OOMs during a 4-hour burn-in with representative traffic.\\n   - KV-cache eviction patterns are compatible (see KV cache compatibility checklist).\\n\\nPreflight checklist (operator)\\n\\n- Operator ownership: assign a primary operator and a secondary on-call.\\n- Artifact verification: verify model bundle signature and provenance chain (SHA256 + cosign signature).\\n- Quantization profile: confirm quantization YAML is present and matches runtime capability matrix.\\n- Runtime compatibility table: confirm target runtime binaries (libredwood_runtime.so) and kernel variants are present for target hardware.\\n- Customer telemetry contract: confirm telemetry level required by customer (sampling rate, PII redaction) is enabled.\\n\\nMinimum test matrix (must pass all items)\\n\\n| Test case | Description | Acceptance |\\n|---|---:|---|\\n| Unit smoke | Load model, run a minimal token generation | returns tokens, no errors |\\n| Synthetic throughput | Run load generator (k6/locust) at target qps | throughput within 10% |\\n| 4-hour burn-in | Continuous traffic representative of production | no crashes, no OOM |\\n| Prompt-set regression | Run customer prompt set (50\\u2013200 prompts) | quality thresholds met |\\n| Embedding parity | 1000 sample vectors from customer corpus | cosine >= 0.985 |\\n| KV-cache survival | Warm cache then run eviction scenarios | no correctness issues |\\n| Telemetry sanity | Ensure traces, metrics, and logs emitted | sample rate observed |\\n\\nStaged rollout plan (recommended)\\n\\n1) Canary (internal): deploy quantized variant into an isolated canary tenant on the same hardware family.\\n   - Duration: 6\\u201312 hours of synthetic + limited real traffic.\\n   - Validation: monitor latency p95, error rate, resource metrics.\\n\\n2) Customer trial: enable quantized variant for 1\\u20133 low-risk customer tenants with automatic fallback to baseline if metrics cross thresholds.\\n   - Duration: 24\\u201372 hours.\\n   - Operators should run the prompt-set regression daily and compare results to baseline.\\n\\n3) Gradual fan-out: increase tenant count by factors of 2 every 24 hours while monitoring.\\n\\n4) Cutover: after 1 week of steady metrics, allow customer to opt in for full conversion. Maintain a 48-hour manual-backout window.\\n\\nOperator rollout commands (examples)\\n\\n- Verify artifact signature:\\n\\n```\\nsha256sum model.quantized.tar.gz\\ncosign verify --key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/model-signing model.quantized.tar.gz\\n```\\n\\n- Stage to canary runtime:\\n\\n```\\nredwoodctl deploy model --bundle model.quantized.tar.gz --profile quant-profile.yaml --target canary-tenant --strategy staged\\n```\\n\\n- Activate trial for customer tenant (example):\\n\\n```\\nredwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-quant --rollout 10%\\n```\\n\\nRollback triggers and automation\\n\\nAutomated rollback should trigger when any of the following are observed for the affected tenant(s) within a 30-minute window unless overridden by a named approver: \\n\\n- p95 latency > configured SLO + 25% for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.\\n- Error rate increase >= 1 percentage point and absolute error rate > 0.5% (application-level errors).\\n- Quality regression observed on daily prompt-set exceeding acceptance thresholds.\\n- Any hard runtime crash (segfault, driver panic, fatal kernel error).\\n\\nRollback steps (manual override)\\n\\n1) Pause new traffic to the quantized variant: \\n   - redwoodctl rollout pause --model model-v2-quant --tenant tenant-1234\\n2) Re-route traffic to previous model:\\n   - redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-baseline --rollout 100%\\n3) Preserve artifacts and logs: collect model bundle, runtime logs, and kernel traces and attach to incident ticket.\\n4) If kernel/driver panic suspected, escalate to infra and file a field incident with detailed environment capture (dmesg, nvml logs, kernel oops)\\n\\nKV cache compatibility notes\\n\\n- Quantized models may change KV cache layout if activations are stored in lower precision. The runtime includes an on-disk compatibility tag at model bundle root: `kv_cache_compat: v2`. Operators must verify that target runtime supports the tag.\\n- If tag mismatch is detected, the runtime will refuse to mount existing cache by default; to preserve cold-start behavior, perform a warm-up pass to rebuild KV caches.\\n\\nQuantization profile example (quant-profile.yaml)\\n\\n```\\nmodel:\\n  name: model-v2\\n  variant: int8-quant\\nquantization:\\n  algorithm: blockwise-8bit\\n  per_channel: true\\n  calibration: dynamic\\nruntime_requirements:\\n  - kernel_variant: f16-accel-h100\\n  - min_compute_capability: 8.0\\n  - kv_cache_compat: \\\"v2\\\"\\nperf_expectation:\\n  p95_latency_pct_increase: 12\\n  throughput_drop_pct: 7\\n```\\n\\nTelemetry & SLOs to monitor\\n\\n- Metrics (emit at request-token granularity): request_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, gpu_memory_bytes_total, kernel_errors.count\\n- Traces: sampling for cold-start request and first 10 tokens; attach model_id and quant_profile label.\\n- Logs: structured operation logs including artifact_sha, operator_id, tenant_id, node_id.\\n- Alert thresholds (suggested):\\n  - latency_p95 > baseline*1.25 -> Sev3 alert to oncall + operator\\n  - kernel_errors.count > 0 -> Sev2, immediate paging to infra\\n  - quality_regression.daily > threshold -> owner notification and ops review\\n\\nEvidence for customer acceptance handoff\\n\\n- Signed model bundle + checksum file.\\n- Burn-in run report (CSV) with latency, throughput, memory, and error metrics.\\n- Prompt-set regression report (diffs and sample outputs).\\n- Embedding parity report (summary stats and histogram).\\n- Telemetry contract verification (sampling rate and PII redaction snapshot).\\n\\nOperator escalation matrix\\n\\n1) Operator on-call (primary) \\u2014 troubleshoot and execute rollback if needed.\\n2) Platform SRE \\u2014 investigate kernel/driver failures.\\n3) Solutions Engineer (customer-facing) \\u2014 coordinate customer communication.\\n4) Security/Legal (if telemetry/PII exposure suspected)\\n\\nPostmortem and evidence preservation\\n\\n- If rollback occurs, create a postmortem within 72 hours including timeline, root cause hypothesis, and mitigations. Attach: model bundle, runtime logs, kernel traces, alert graphs, and the acceptance test artifacts.\\n\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Example prompt-set regression runner (CLI)\\n\\n```\\n# run prompt-set and produce CSV diff\\npython tools/prompt_regression_runner.py \\\\\\n  --model-endpoint https://private-runner.local/tenants/tenant-1234/model-v2-quant \\\\\\n  --prompts prompts/customer-critical-50.json \\\\\\n  --output reports/quant_regression.csv\\n```\\n\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Common failure modes and mitigations\\n\\n- Symptom: p95 latency spikes after quantized rollout.\\n  - Likely causes: suboptimal kernel variant selected, increased serialization overhead, or KV-cache rebuilds.\\n  - Mitigation: pin alternative kernel_variant in runtime config, increase batching window temporarily, or roll back.\\n\\n- Symptom: embedding cosine drift below threshold.\\n  - Likely causes: calibration dataset mismatch or per-channel quantization error.\\n  - Mitigation: re-run calibration with customer corpus, increase calibration samples, or disable per_channel quantization.\\n\\n- Symptom: GPU OOMs on some nodes only.\\n  - Likely causes: driver/kernel mismatch or firmware variation.\\n  - Mitigation: isolate affected nodes, run driver/firmware validation harness, move tenants off node.\\n\\nOwners and contacts\\n\\n- Document owner: Ava Patel (eng-serving-runtime) \\u2014 ava.patel@redwood.ai\\n- Primary SRE contact: Miguel Santos \\u2014 miguel.santos@redwood.ai\\n- Solutions Engineer lead: Lina Zhou \\u2014 lina.zhou@redwood.ai\\n\\nRelated reading\\n\\n- See also on-prem packaging and air-gap artifact delivery, KV cache migration playbooks, and the runtime kernel compatibility matrix.\\n\\nChange log\\n\\n- 2026-01-12: Initial draft created by Ava Patel.\\n- 2026-04-07: Added KV cache compatibility section and automated rollback triggers (reviewers: Miguel Santos).\\n- 2026-06-10: Finalized acceptance thresholds and appended CLI examples (publish).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a1bd525bf3ef484d9aa37b4b3f63f98c\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Model quantization and compatibility — customer readiness checklist & operator playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/model-quantization-and-compatibility-customer-readiness-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\nsuspected, escalate to infra and file a field incident with detailed environment capture ( dmesg, nvml logs, kernel oops ) kv cache compatibility notes - quantized models may change kv cache layout if activations are stored in lower precision. the runtime includes an on - disk compatibility tag at model bundle root : ` kv _ cache _ compat : v2 `. operators must verify that target runtime supports the tag. - if tag mismatch is detected, the runtime will refuse to mount existing cache by default ; to preserve cold - start behavior, perform a warm - up pass to rebuild kv caches. quantization profile example ( quant - profile. yaml )",

document.title: Model quantization and compatibility — customer readiness checklist & operator playbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "Model quantization and compatibility — customer readiness checklist & operator playbook",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Ava Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-12",
  "last_updated": "2026-06-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Miguel Santos",
    "Lina Zhou",
    "Rajiv Menon"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "quantization",
    "private-deploy",
    "compatibility",
    "operator-playbook",
    "acceptance-tests"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026",
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "content": "Overview

This page describes the customer-facing requirements and the operator runbook for performing model quantization and compatibility validation in Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It covers acceptance criteria, staged rollout steps, preflight checks, monitoring thresholds, and explicit rollback triggers. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable process that protects customer SLAs and preserves model quality while enabling cost-efficient quantized execution on heterogeneous GPU/CPU fleets.

Scope

- Applies to model artifact updates that introduce any quantized weight formats (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, or mixed-precision) or kernel ABI changes that affect runtime compatibility.
- Targets Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Hosted/Dedicated customers should reference the hosted quantization guidance instead.
- Intended audience: Field operators, SRE/Platform on-call, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success engineers during handoffs.

Why this matters

- Quantization reduces memory and cost but can alter numeric characteristics and performance. A structured validation prevents regressions in latency, throughput, and output quality.
- Private deployments often contain heterogeneous accelerators (A100, H100, inferred ARM CPUs). Compatibility mismatches occur when kernels or compilation artifacts do not match target microarchitectures.

Acceptance Criteria (customer-facing)

Use the following acceptance thresholds for a quantized model variant to be considered "ready" for staged rollout to production tenants: 

1) Quality (functional):
   - Task accuracy / F1 / BLEU / ROUGE: not worse than baseline model by more than 1.5 absolute points for critical prompt set; or relative drop <= 3% if metric is ratio-based.
   - Latent semantic similarity (embedding-based): average cosine similarity to baseline embeddings >= 0.985 on the customer prompt set.

2) Latency and throughput:
   - p95 generation latency at customer sequence length baseline: increase <= 15% compared to baseline run.
   - Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <= 10% under the target batch profile.

3) Resource and thermal behavior:
   - GPU memory usage reduced as expected by quantization profile (documented in the quant-profile YAML).
   - No sustained thermal throttling or preemption events during synthetic burn-in runs.

4) Stability:
   - No hard crashes, CUDA driver errors, or kernel OOMs during a 4-hour burn-in with representative traffic.
   - KV-cache eviction patterns are compatible (see KV cache compatibility checklist).

Preflight checklist (operator)

- Operator ownership: assign a primary operator and a secondary on-call.
- Artifact verification: verify model bundle signature and provenance chain (SHA256 + cosign signature).
- Quantization profile: confirm quantization YAML is present and matches runtime capability matrix.
- Runtime compatibility table: confirm target runtime binaries (libredwood_runtime.so) and kernel variants are present for target hardware.
- Customer telemetry contract: confirm telemetry level required by customer (sampling rate, PII redaction) is enabled.

Minimum test matrix (must pass all items)

| Test case | Description | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Unit smoke | Load model, run a minimal token generation | returns tokens, no errors |
| Synthetic throughput | Run load generator (k6/locust) at target qps | throughput within 10% |
| 4-hour burn-in | Continuous traffic representative of production | no crashes, no OOM |
| Prompt-set regression | Run customer prompt set (50–200 prompts) | quality thresholds met |
| Embedding parity | 1000 sample vectors from customer corpus | cosine >= 0.985 |
| KV-cache survival | Warm cache then run eviction scenarios | no correctness issues |
| Telemetry sanity | Ensure traces, metrics, and logs emitted | sample rate observed |

Staged rollout plan (recommended)

1) Canary (internal): deploy quantized variant into an isolated canary tenant on the same hardware family.
   - Duration: 6–12 hours of synthetic + limited real traffic.
   - Validation: monitor latency p95, error rate, resource metrics.

2) Customer trial: enable quantized variant for 1–3 low-risk customer tenants with automatic fallback to baseline if metrics cross thresholds.
   - Duration: 24–72 hours.
   - Operators should run the prompt-set regression daily and compare results to baseline.

3) Gradual fan-out: increase tenant count by factors of 2 every 24 hours while monitoring.

4) Cutover: after 1 week of steady metrics, allow customer to opt in for full conversion. Maintain a 48-hour manual-backout window.

Operator rollout commands (examples)

- Verify artifact signature:

```
sha256sum model.quantized.tar.gz
cosign verify --key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/model-signing model.quantized.tar.gz
```

- Stage to canary runtime:

```
redwoodctl deploy model --bundle model.quantized.tar.gz --profile quant-profile.yaml --target canary-tenant --strategy staged
```

- Activate trial for customer tenant (example):

```
redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-quant --rollout 10%
```

Rollback triggers and automation

Automated rollback should trigger when any of the following are observed for the affected tenant(s) within a 30-minute window unless overridden by a named approver: 

- p95 latency > configured SLO + 25% for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Error rate increase >= 1 percentage point and absolute error rate > 0.5% (application-level errors).
- Quality regression observed on daily prompt-set exceeding acceptance thresholds.
- Any hard runtime crash (segfault, driver panic, fatal kernel error).

Rollback steps (manual override)

1) Pause new traffic to the quantized variant: 
   - redwoodctl rollout pause --model model-v2-quant --tenant tenant-1234
2) Re-route traffic to previous model:
   - redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-baseline --rollout 100%
3) Preserve artifacts and logs: collect model bundle, runtime logs, and kernel traces and attach to incident ticket.
4) If kernel/driver panic suspected, escalate to infra and file a field incident with detailed environment capture (dmesg, nvml logs, kernel oops)

KV cache compatibility notes

- Quantized models may change KV cache layout if activations are stored in lower precision. The runtime includes an on-disk compatibility tag at model bundle root: `kv_cache_compat: v2`. Operators must verify that target runtime supports the tag.
- If tag mismatch is detected, the runtime will refuse to mount existing cache by default; to preserve cold-start behavior, perform a warm-up pass to rebuild KV caches.

Quantization profile example (quant-profile.yaml)

```
model:
  name: model-v2
  variant: int8-quant
quantization:
  algorithm: blockwise-8bit
  per_channel: true
  calibration: dynamic
runtime_requirements:
  - kernel_variant: f16-accel-h100
  - min_compute_capability: 8.0
  - kv_cache_compat: "v2"
perf_expectation:
  p95_latency_pct_increase: 12
  throughput_drop_pct: 7
```

Telemetry & SLOs to monitor

- Metrics (emit at request-token granularity): request_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, gpu_memory_bytes_total, kernel_errors.count
- Traces: sampling for cold-start request and first 10 tokens; attach model_id and quant_profile label.
- Logs: structured operation logs including artifact_sha, operator_id, tenant_id, node_id.
- Alert thresholds (suggested):
  - latency_p95 > baseline*1.25 -> Sev3 alert to oncall + operator
  - kernel_errors.count > 0 -> Sev2, immediate paging to infra
  - quality_regression.daily > threshold -> owner notification and ops review

Evidence for customer acceptance handoff

- Signed model bundle + checksum file.
- Burn-in run report (CSV) with latency, throughput, memory, and error metrics.
- Prompt-set regression report (diffs and sample outputs).
- Embedding parity report (summary stats and histogram).
- Telemetry contract verification (sampling rate and PII redaction snapshot).

Operator escalation matrix

1) Operator on-call (primary) — troubleshoot and execute rollback if needed.
2) Platform SRE — investigate kernel/driver failures.
3) Solutions Engineer (customer-facing) — coordinate customer communication.
4) Security/Legal (if telemetry/PII exposure suspected)

Postmortem and evidence preservation

- If rollback occurs, create a postmortem within 72 hours including timeline, root cause hypothesis, and mitigations. Attach: model bundle, runtime logs, kernel traces, alert graphs, and the acceptance test artifacts.

Appendix A — Example prompt-set regression runner (CLI)

```
# run prompt-set and produce CSV diff
python tools/prompt_regression_runner.py \
  --model-endpoint https://private-runner.local/tenants/tenant-1234/model-v2-quant \
  --prompts prompts/customer-critical-50.json \
  --output reports/quant_regression.csv
```

Appendix B — Common failure modes and mitigations

- Symptom: p95 latency spikes after quantized rollout.
  - Likely causes: suboptimal kernel variant selected, increased serialization overhead, or KV-cache rebuilds.
  - Mitigation: pin alternative kernel_variant in runtime config, increase batching window temporarily, or roll back.

- Symptom: embedding cosine drift below threshold.
  - Likely causes: calibration dataset mismatch or per-channel quantization error.
  - Mitigation: re-run calibration with customer corpus, increase calibration samples, or disable per_channel quantization.

- Symptom: GPU OOMs on some nodes only.
  - Likely causes: driver/kernel mismatch or firmware variation.
  - Mitigation: isolate affected nodes, run driver/firmware validation harness, move tenants off node.

Owners and contacts

- Document owner: Ava Patel (eng-serving-runtime) — ava.patel@redwood.ai
- Primary SRE contact: Miguel Santos — miguel.santos@redwood.ai
- Solutions Engineer lead: Lina Zhou — lina.zhou@redwood.ai

Related reading

- See also on-prem packaging and air-gap artifact delivery, KV cache migration playbooks, and the runtime kernel compatibility matrix.

Change log

- 2026-01-12: Initial draft created by Ava Patel.
- 2026-04-07: Added KV cache compatibility section and automated rollback triggers (reviewers: Miguel Santos).
- 2026-06-10: Finalized acceptance thresholds and appended CLI examples (publish).

    "id": "dsid_ceff8cd25c714f5faf8052f59e580184",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/heterogeneous-quantization-compatibility-bench-and-gate-2026.json",
    "title": "heterogeneous-quantization-compatibility-bench-and-gate-2026",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"heterogeneous-quantization-compatibility-bench-and-gate-2026\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-serving-runtime\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-05\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Marco Nguyen\",\n    \"Elena Karpova\",\n    \"Diego Ramos\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"benchmark\",\n    \"quantization\",\n    \"compatibility\",\n    \"perf-gating\",\n    \"gpu\",\n    \"fidelity\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"../profiling-playbook/quantization-timing-investigation-handbook-2026\",\n    \"../kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-compat-matrix-and-rolling-upgrade-playbook-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Summary:\\nThis playbook documents the benchmarking harness, pass/fail gating criteria, and rollout procedures for deploying heterogeneous quantized model variants across the Redwood serving runtime. It covers functional compatibility checks, latency/throughput regressions, scheduler interactions, and trace/telemetry expectations when enabling INT8/INT4/mixed quantized kernels across different accelerator families.\\n\\nContext and motivation:\\n- Quantization reduces per-token cost but interacts with kernel selection, KV cache semantics, and scheduler admission.\\n- Different hardware (A100, H100, A10G, RTX series) and driver/toolkit combinations expose subtle numerical and perf differences.\\n- We need an automated, reproducible bench and gate so that quantized rollouts do not cause silent quality regressions or operational instability.\\n\\nScope:\\n- Model families: decoder-only LLMs currently in serving fleet (7B\\u201370B variants).\\n- Quant schemes: symmetric asymmetric INT8, dynamic/quant-aware INT4, group-wise per-channel scales, and mixed fp16/INT8 kernels.\\n- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 (40/80GB), H100 (80GB), A10G, and representative on-prem RTX6000-class nodes.\\n- Runtime surfaces: kernel selection path, KV cache behavior, session warmstart, scheduler handoff.\\n\\nBench objectives and primary metrics:\\n- Correctness: token-level output equivalence check (soft) against fp16 baseline using perplexity and distributional drift metrics. Gate: top-1 token divergence <= 0.8% and log-prob drift RMS <= 0.12.\\n- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for generation with 32-token completions. Gate: p95 <= baseline_p95 + 12ms on same hardware class.\\n- Throughput: tokens/sec under continuous steady-state. Gate: throughput drop <= 15% vs baseline for same sequence-length distribution.\\n- Resource safety: GPU memory delta, peak SM utilization, and thermal/power events. Gate: memory overhead <= +2GB for same shard placement; no thermal throttling during 1h soak.\\n- Scheduler impact: admission/queue time distribution and preemption events. Gate: queue-time p95 regression <= 10ms and preempt rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points.\\n\\nTest harness and reproducibility:\\n- All bench runs are executed through the bench-orchestrator container with version-tagged artifacts. Typical CLI:\\n  ./bench-orchestrator run --suite quant-compat --model gpt-redwood-13b --variant int8-symmetric --hw a100-80 --seed 42 --duration 3600 --trace true\\n\\n- Example orchestration config (YAML) used for reproducible runs (presented as plain text):\\n  ---\\n  suite: quant-compat\\n  model: gpt-redwood-13b\\n  variants: [fp16, int8-symmetric, int4-mixed]\\n  hardware: [a100-80, a10g, h100-80]\\n  sequence_profile: \\\"web-chat-32-32\\\"\\n  duration_seconds: 3600\\n  traffic_shape: \\\"steady\\\"\\n  trace_level: \\\"full\\\"\\n  metrics_to_collect: [latency, throughput, logprobs, kernel_signals, scheduler_telemetry]\\n  ---\\n\\nWorkload definitions (catalog):\\n- web-chat-32-32: prompt len=32, gen len=32, 1 request per second per client, 200 clients.\\n- long-infer-128: prompt len=128, gen len=128, low concurrency (20 clients), used to stress KV cache.\\n- bursty-batch: synthetic burst bursts to validate admission controller and kernel preemption.\\n\\nHardware matrix (table):\\n| hardware | driver | cuda | cudnn | notes |\\n| A100-80 | 525.60 | 11.8 | 8.4 | baseline fleet node |\\n| H100-80 | 535.54 | 12.1 | 8.5 | large-model heavy kernel variants |\\n| A10G | 520.56 | 11.7 | 8.3 | cost-optimized host |\\n| RTX6000 | 515.43 | 11.6 | 8.2 | on-prem reference |\\n\\nQuantization profiles exercised (examples):\\n- int8-symmetric: per-tensor symmetric scales, fused matmul-kernel path.\\n- int8-perchannel: per-output channel scales, preferred for grouped conv-like operations in some kernels.\\n- int4-mixed: kv cache keys stored in INT8, weights int4 with fp16 accumulation for matmuls.\\n- dynamic-qat: quantization-aware fine-tuning enabled with 128-step calibration.\\n\\nQuality and numerical checks (procedure):\\n1. Run correctness harness on a 2k-sample reference corpus (reserved eval set). Collect logits, prefix logprobs, and argmax tokens.\\n2. Compute metrics: token divergence (fraction of tokens where argmax changes), KL divergence of softmax distributions, and RMS log-prob drift.\\n3. If token divergence > 0.8% OR KL > 0.05 OR RMS drift > 0.12, mark the variant FAILED and abort rollout.\\n\\nPerformance and operational checks (procedure):\\n1. Warmup: run 15-minute warmup under workload profile. Verify KV cache warm-up completion and shader JIT stabilization.\\n2. Soak: 1-hour steady-state run. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory, and scheduler traces.\\n3. Failure modes monitored: out-of-memory, kernel launch timeouts, driver resets, and excessive preempt/backpressure events.\\n4. If any hard failure occurs (OOM, driver reset), variant is FAILED automatically.\\n\\nScheduler interaction tests (special):\\n- Run mixed cohort where 20% of requests use quantized variant and 80% use fp16 to validate admission controller smoothing. Observe admission tokens/sec variance and kernel handoff latency.\\n- Inject synthetic priority inversion by marking high-priority low-latency requests during burst windows; measure end-to-end impact.\\n\\nAcceptance gates and rollout matrix:\\n- Canary (10% traffic, single region): pass all correctness checks, p95 <= baseline_p95+12ms, thermal/power stable.\\n- Regional wave (50% traffic across 2 AZs): no more than 0.5% customer-visible error increase during 24h, scheduler preempt increase <= 0.5pp.\\n- Fleet roll (100%): no regressions observed in 72h aggregated metrics; manual sign-off by runtime and SRE owners.\\n\\nRollout checklist (numbered steps):\\n1. Validate bench artifacts and record full trace URLs in the release ticket.\\n2. Run local preflight on representative dev nodes (10 minutes).\\n3. Submit canary binary and kernel hints to canary pool.\\n4. Monitor canary with enhanced telemetry (kernel-level traces, perf counters, trace-sampling=10%).\\n5. If canary passes 12h check, advance to regional wave, else rollback immediately using kernel rollback playbook.\\n6. Post regional wave soak, check quality regressions with reference eval set.\\n7. Fleet roll and final sign-off.\\n\\nObservability and traces to collect (minimum):\\n- kernel_id, kernel_variant, kernel_duration_ms, kernel_queue_time_ms\\n- kvcache_warmup_percent, kvcache_miss_rate, kvcache_eviction_count\\n- preempt_event_count, admission_queue_time_ms, scheduling_slot_id\\n- per-token logprob delta (sampled 0.5% of requests)\\n\\nAutomated alarms (suggested):\\n- token_divergence_rate > 0.8% over a 30-minute window -> Pager -> owners: runtime-team@s.redwood.ai\\n- p95 latency regression > 12ms for 10-minute window -> Pager -> owners: sre-oncall@s.redwood.ai\\n- OOM or driver-reset event count > 1 in 1 hour -> Immediate rollback and incident creation.\\n\\nOwnership and escalation:\\n- Bench harness owner: Performance Engineering (Primary: Marco Nguyen).\\n- Rollout owner: Runtime Releases (Primary: Elena Karpova).\\n- Oncall escalation: Eng-SRE -> Runtime leads -> Applied ML if model quality suspicion.\\n\\nAppendix A: Example analysis commands\\n- Extract top divergent prompts:\\n  python scripts/analysis/top_divergent_prompts.py --baseline traces/fp16-run.json --variant traces/int8-run.json --out reports/divergent.csv\\n- Kernel-level flamegraph generation:\\n  perf-kernel-collector --input traces/kernel-events.ndjson --output flame.svg --group-by kernel_variant\\n\\nAppendix B: Known caveats and mitigation notes\\n- Some older driver stacks return non-deterministic host-side rounding for INT4 accumulators; avoid enabling int4-mixed on nodes with driver < 520.70.\\n- KV cache pointer packing in int4 modes increases reconstruction cost during warmstart; add an extra warmup pass for long-infer workloads.\\n- Scheduler fairness heuristics may favor fp16 kernels due to lower variance; ensure admission controller accounts for measured variance in tokens/sec estimates.\\n\\nChange log:\\n- 2024-11-05 (Aisha Patel): Initial draft and bench harness definition.\\n- 2025-06-02 (Marco Nguyen): Added scheduler interaction tests and acceptance gates.\\n- 2026-01-12 (Elena Karpova): Revised numerical gate thresholds and hardware matrix to include H100.\\n\\nRelated documents and links:\\n- Quantization rollout safety playbook: ../runbooks/quantization-rollout-safety-and-quality-gate-playbook-2026\\n- Kernel compatibility matrix: ../kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-compat-matrix-and-rolling-upgrade-playbook-2026\\n\\nIf you run this playbook, capture an experiment ticket with the bench-orchestrator run-id and attach all traces. For questions or clarifications, ping the performance-engineering channel on Slack (team-perf@s.redwood.ai).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_ceff8cd25c714f5faf8052f59e580184\"\n}",

{
  "title": "heterogeneous-quantization-compatibility-bench-and-gate-2026",
  "space": "eng-serving-runtime",
  "author": "Aisha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-05",
  "last_updated": "2026-01-12",
  "reviewers": [
    "Marco Nguyen",
    "Elena Karpova",
    "Diego Ramos"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "benchmark",
    "quantization",
    "compatibility",
    "perf-gating",
    "gpu",
    "fidelity"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "../profiling-playbook/quantization-timing-investigation-handbook-2026",
    "../kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-compat-matrix-and-rolling-upgrade-playbook-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Summary:
This playbook documents the benchmarking harness, pass/fail gating criteria, and rollout procedures for deploying heterogeneous quantized model variants across the Redwood serving runtime. It covers functional compatibility checks, latency/throughput regressions, scheduler interactions, and trace/telemetry expectations when enabling INT8/INT4/mixed quantized kernels across different accelerator families.

Context and motivation:
- Quantization reduces per-token cost but interacts with kernel selection, KV cache semantics, and scheduler admission.
- Different hardware (A100, H100, A10G, RTX series) and driver/toolkit combinations expose subtle numerical and perf differences.
- We need an automated, reproducible bench and gate so that quantized rollouts do not cause silent quality regressions or operational instability.

Scope:
- Model families: decoder-only LLMs currently in serving fleet (7B–70B variants).
- Quant schemes: symmetric asymmetric INT8, dynamic/quant-aware INT4, group-wise per-channel scales, and mixed fp16/INT8 kernels.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 (40/80GB), H100 (80GB), A10G, and representative on-prem RTX6000-class nodes.
- Runtime surfaces: kernel selection path, KV cache behavior, session warmstart, scheduler handoff.

Bench objectives and primary metrics:
- Correctness: token-level output equivalence check (soft) against fp16 baseline using perplexity and distributional drift metrics. Gate: top-1 token divergence <= 0.8% and log-prob drift RMS <= 0.12.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for generation with 32-token completions. Gate: p95 <= baseline_p95 + 12ms on same hardware class.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under continuous steady-state. Gate: throughput drop <= 15% vs baseline for same sequence-length distribution.
- Resource safety: GPU memory delta, peak SM utilization, and thermal/power events. Gate: memory overhead <= +2GB for same shard placement; no thermal throttling during 1h soak.
- Scheduler impact: admission/queue time distribution and preemption events. Gate: queue-time p95 regression <= 10ms and preempt rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points.

Test harness and reproducibility:
- All bench runs are executed through the bench-orchestrator container with version-tagged artifacts. Typical CLI:
  ./bench-orchestrator run --suite quant-compat --model gpt-redwood-13b --variant int8-symmetric --hw a100-80 --seed 42 --duration 3600 --trace true

- Example orchestration config (YAML) used for reproducible runs (presented as plain text):
  ---
  suite: quant-compat
  model: gpt-redwood-13b
  variants: [fp16, int8-symmetric, int4-mixed]
  hardware: [a100-80, a10g, h100-80]
  sequence_profile: "web-chat-32-32"
  duration_seconds: 3600
  traffic_shape: "steady"
  trace_level: "full"
  metrics_to_collect: [latency, throughput, logprobs, kernel_signals, scheduler_telemetry]
  ---

Workload definitions (catalog):
- web-chat-32-32: prompt len=32, gen len=32, 1 request per second per client, 200 clients.
- long-infer-128: prompt len=128, gen len=128, low concurrency (20 clients), used to stress KV cache.
- bursty-batch: synthetic burst bursts to validate admission controller and kernel preemption.

Hardware matrix (table):
| hardware | driver | cuda | cudnn | notes |
| A100-80 | 525.60 | 11.8 | 8.4 | baseline fleet node |
| H100-80 | 535.54 | 12.1 | 8.5 | large-model heavy kernel variants |
| A10G | 520.56 | 11.7 | 8.3 | cost-optimized host |
| RTX6000 | 515.43 | 11.6 | 8.2 | on-prem reference |

Quantization profiles exercised (examples):
- int8-symmetric: per-tensor symmetric scales, fused matmul-kernel path.
- int8-perchannel: per-output channel scales, preferred for grouped conv-like operations in some kernels.
- int4-mixed: kv cache keys stored in INT8, weights int4 with fp16 accumulation for matmuls.
- dynamic-qat: quantization-aware fine-tuning enabled with 128-step calibration.

Quality and numerical checks (procedure):
1. Run correctness harness on a 2k-sample reference corpus (reserved eval set). Collect logits, prefix logprobs, and argmax tokens.
2. Compute metrics: token divergence (fraction of tokens where argmax changes), KL divergence of softmax distributions, and RMS log-prob drift.
3. If token divergence > 0.8% OR KL > 0.05 OR RMS drift > 0.12, mark the variant FAILED and abort rollout.

Performance and operational checks (procedure):
1. Warmup: run 15-minute warmup under workload profile. Verify KV cache warm-up completion and shader JIT stabilization.
2. Soak: 1-hour steady-state run. Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory, and scheduler traces.
3. Failure modes monitored: out-of-memory, kernel launch timeouts, driver resets, and excessive preempt/backpressure events.
4. If any hard failure occurs (OOM, driver reset), variant is FAILED automatically.

Scheduler interaction tests (special):
- Run mixed cohort where 20% of requests use quantized variant and 80% use fp16 to validate admission controller smoothing. Observe admission tokens/sec variance and kernel handoff latency.
- Inject synthetic priority inversion by marking high-priority low-latency requests during burst windows; measure end-to-end impact.

Acceptance gates and rollout matrix:
- Canary (10% traffic, single region): pass all correctness checks, p95 <= baseline_p95+12ms, thermal/power stable.
- Regional wave (50% traffic across 2 AZs): no more than 0.5% customer-visible error increase during 24h, scheduler preempt increase <= 0.5pp.
- Fleet roll (100%): no regressions observed in 72h aggregated metrics; manual sign-off by runtime and SRE owners.

Rollout checklist (numbered steps):
1. Validate bench artifacts and record full trace URLs in the release ticket.
2. Run local preflight on representative dev nodes (10 minutes).
3. Submit canary binary and kernel hints to canary pool.
4. Monitor canary with enhanced telemetry (kernel-level traces, perf counters, trace-sampling=10%).
5. If canary passes 12h check, advance to regional wave, else rollback immediately using kernel rollback playbook.
6. Post regional wave soak, check quality regressions with reference eval set.
7. Fleet roll and final sign-off.

Observability and traces to collect (minimum):
- kernel_id, kernel_variant, kernel_duration_ms, kernel_queue_time_ms
- kvcache_warmup_percent, kvcache_miss_rate, kvcache_eviction_count
- preempt_event_count, admission_queue_time_ms, scheduling_slot_id
- per-token logprob delta (sampled 0.5% of requests)

Automated alarms (suggested):
- token_divergence_rate > 0.8% over a 30-minute window -> Pager -> owners: runtime-team@s.redwood.ai
- p95 latency regression > 12ms for 10-minute window -> Pager -> owners: sre-oncall@s.redwood.ai
- OOM or driver-reset event count > 1 in 1 hour -> Immediate rollback and incident creation.

Ownership and escalation:
- Bench harness owner: Performance Engineering (Primary: Marco Nguyen).
- Rollout owner: Runtime Releases (Primary: Elena Karpova).
- Oncall escalation: Eng-SRE -> Runtime leads -> Applied ML if model quality suspicion.

Appendix A: Example analysis commands
- Extract top divergent prompts:
  python scripts/analysis/top_divergent_prompts.py --baseline traces/fp16-run.json --variant traces/int8-run.json --out reports/divergent.csv
- Kernel-level flamegraph generation:
  perf-kernel-collector --input traces/kernel-events.ndjson --output flame.svg --group-by kernel_variant

Appendix B: Known caveats and mitigation notes
- Some older driver stacks return non-deterministic host-side rounding for INT4 accumulators; avoid enabling int4-mixed on nodes with driver < 520.70.
- KV cache pointer packing in int4 modes increases reconstruction cost during warmstart; add an extra warmup pass for long-infer workloads.
- Scheduler fairness heuristics may favor fp16 kernels due to lower variance; ensure admission controller accounts for measured variance in tokens/sec estimates.

Change log:
- 2024-11-05 (Aisha Patel): Initial draft and bench harness definition.
- 2025-06-02 (Marco Nguyen): Added scheduler interaction tests and acceptance gates.
- 2026-01-12 (Elena Karpova): Revised numerical gate thresholds and hardware matrix to include H100.

Related documents and links:
- Quantization rollout safety playbook: ../runbooks/quantization-rollout-safety-and-quality-gate-playbook-2026
- Kernel compatibility matrix: ../kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-compat-matrix-and-rolling-upgrade-playbook-2026

If you run this playbook, capture an experiment ticket with the bench-orchestrator run-id and attach all traces. For questions or clarifications, ping the performance-engineering channel on Slack (team-perf@s.redwood.ai).

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Rollout Runbook: Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (H100/B200/L40S)\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-serving-runtime\",\n  \"author\": \"Kira Thompson\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-25\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-01-15\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Irene Choi\",\n    \"Aisha Bello\",\n    \"Noah Patel\",\n    \"Sofia Ivanova\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"rollout\",\n    \"serving-runtime\",\n    \"profiles\",\n    \"performance\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"rollback\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/hardware-tuning-profiles-pack-overview\",\n    \"confluence://eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/profile-schema-and-compatibility-rules\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hardware-tuning-profiles-distribution-and-override-order\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/perf-canary-gates-for-hardware-profiles\",\n    \"confluence://eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/hardware-profile-known-issues-and-mitigations\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"h1. Purpose\\nThis runbook describes the operational procedure for safely rolling out the *Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack* for the serving runtime across *Hosted, Dedicated, and Private* deployments. It covers:\\n\\n* Staged rollout by pool/region\\n* Required dashboards and gates\\n* Alert thresholds and stop/rollback criteria\\n* Triage and incident response playbook for regressions\\n\\nThe profiles pack provides curated, versioned runtime configuration presets per GPU SKU (*H100, B200, L40S*) and a consistent override model across fleet defaults and per-deployment overrides.\\n\\nh1. Scope and assumptions\\nh2. In scope\\n* Enabling a specific *profile pack version* as the fleet default (or per-pool override)\\n* Enabling/disabling the profiles feature at runtime\\n* Rolling forward/back profile versions\\n* Handling expected failure modes: performance regressions, OOMs, elevated error rate, queueing/backpressure anomalies, profile mis-detection\\n\\nh2. Out of scope\\n* Customer-specific bespoke tuning beyond supported overrides (route-level overrides handled via Support/Solutions)\\n* Writing new kernels (kernel changes should have separate rollout/guardrail docs)\\n\\nh2. Definitions\\n* *Profile pack* \\u2014 Versioned bundle of hardware tuning profiles.\\n* *Selected profile* \\u2014 The runtime\\u2019s chosen profile after hardware detection and compatibility checks.\\n* *Override order* \\u2014 Precedence rules (fleet default, per-pool, per-deployment Helm values/env, per-route policy, etc.). See ADR.\\n* *Canary pool* \\u2014 Small percentage of traffic/capacity used for early validation.\\n\\nh1. Ownership and escalation\\n* Primary oncall: *eng-oncall* (Serving Runtime)\\n* SRE escalation: *eng-sre* (Neha Kapoor org) and *#eng-sre-oncall*\\n* Infra/fleet escalation: Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz\\n* Runtime scheduling escalation: Sofia Ivanova / Lena Fischer / Marcus Reed\\n* Kernel tuning escalation: Hiro Tanaka / Yuki Sato / Grace Kim\\n\\nh2. Change approvers (rollout sign-off)\\n* SRE: Sean Gallagher\\n* Infra/Fleet: Irene Choi\\n* Runtime: Noah Patel (or delegate)\\n\\nh1. Preconditions (must be true before any rollout)\\n1) *Compatibility checks are green*\\n* Runtime release includes profile loader + compatibility matrix logging at startup.\\n* Profile pack version is declared compatible with the runtime release target.\\n\\n2) *Observability is in place*\\n* Dashboards and alerts for:\\n  * latency (p50/p95/p99) segmented by profile\\n  * throughput/tokens-per-second segmented by profile\\n  * error rate and retry rate\\n  * OOM / CUDA out-of-memory / allocator failures\\n  * queue depth / backpressure / drop rate\\n  * profile selection metrics (selected_profile, override_source)\\n\\n3) *Perf canary gates are configured*\\n* Pre-merge or pre-deploy canary job runs the workload matrix on the target GPU SKU.\\n* Canary thresholds updated for the profile-enabled build.\\n\\n4) *Rollback mechanism is tested*\\n* Confirm we can disable profiles per pool within 10 minutes.\\n* Confirm we can pin profile pack to prior version within 20 minutes.\\n\\nh1. Required dashboards and where to look\\nh2. Dashboards (must be open during rollout)\\n* *Serving Runtime Overview* (global + by region/pool)\\n  * Request rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency\\n* *Profile Selection & Overrides*\\n  * selected_profile (by pool)\\n  * override_source (fleet default vs per-pool vs deployment override)\\n  * mismatch/unknown-sku count\\n* *Perf & Unit Economics*\\n  * tokens/sec, GPU utilization, kernel time\\n  * cost-per-1K tokens (Hosted), effective throughput (Dedicated)\\n* *Scheduler Health*\\n  * queue depth, batch sizes, prefill/decode fairness, backpressure events\\n* *Memory & Stability*\\n  * KV cache usage, fragmentation indicators, OOM count, CUDA errors\\n\\nh2. Logs (minimum)\\n* Runtime startup log line: profile pack version + compatibility matrix\\n* Per-request debug sampling (if enabled): batch size, seq len bucket, decode concurrency\\n\\nh2. Debug tools\\n* CLI: dump effective runtime config after selection and overrides (useful for Private/Dedicated).\\n* Runtime debug endpoint: expose selected profile + effective key knobs.\\n\\nh1. Rollout strategy overview\\nWe roll out in stages, per GPU SKU, per region/pool, and per deployment mode. *Stop-the-line* if any stop criteria is met.\\n\\nh2. Recommended order\\n1) H100: Hosted canary \\u2192 Hosted 25% \\u2192 Hosted 100% \\u2192 Dedicated pilots \\u2192 wider Dedicated\\n2) L40S: Hosted canary \\u2192 Hosted 50% (smaller fleet) \\u2192 Hosted 100% \\u2192 Dedicated\\n3) B200: *Experimental only*, gated by feature flag + limited regions; do not enable fleet-wide defaults until maturity criteria is met.\\n\\nh2. Rollout stages\\n* Stage 0: Dry run (no traffic)\\n* Stage 1: Canary (1\\u20135% capacity or traffic)\\n* Stage 2: Limited expansion (10\\u201325%)\\n* Stage 3: Majority (50\\u201375%)\\n* Stage 4: Full enablement (100%)\\n* Stage 5: Post-rollout validation + documentation\\n\\nh1. Stage 0 \\u2014 Dry run (no customer impact)\\nGoal: confirm profile selection, override order, and basic stability in a controlled environment.\\n\\nChecklist:\\n1) Deploy runtime build + profile pack to a non-prod or shadow pool.\\n2) Verify startup logs include:\\n   * runtime_version\\n   * profile_pack_version\\n   * sku_detection_result\\n   * selected_profile\\n   * compatibility_result\\n3) Run smoke workload:\\n   * short prompts, long prompts, streaming on/off\\n   * tool-calling style (if supported)\\n4) Confirm no elevated:\\n   * OOM / CUDA errors\\n   * error rate > baseline\\n\\nExit criteria:\\n* Zero OOMs in smoke runs\\n* Error rate within baseline noise\\n* selected_profile matches expected SKU profile\\n\\nh1. Stage 1 \\u2014 Canary rollout (1\\u20135%)\\nGoal: validate real traffic behavior with strict rollback readiness.\\n\\nh2. Setup\\n* Choose canary pools per region (at least one high-traffic and one representative low-traffic region).\\n* Ensure oncall coverage for the full canary window.\\n* Disable concurrent major changes (driver upgrades, scheduler refactors, autoscaling policy changes) in canary pools.\\n\\nh2. Steps\\n1) Enable profiles in canary pool only.\\n2) Confirm profile selection is stable (no flapping between profiles across restarts).\\n3) Monitor for 60\\u2013120 minutes (minimum) or 2 peak traffic cycles (recommended).\\n\\nh2. Canary success criteria (must hold)\\n* Latency:\\n  * p95 <= baseline + 5% (same route/model cohort)\\n  * p99 <= baseline + 8%\\n  * No new long-tail spikes correlated with profile selection\\n* Errors:\\n  * 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.1% absolute\\n  * Retry rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute\\n* Stability:\\n  * OOM count == 0 for canary window (or <= baseline if baseline non-zero due to known noisy workloads)\\n* Throughput:\\n  * tokens/sec >= baseline - 2% (we accept small drops if latency improves)\\n\\nh2. Stop criteria (immediate)\\nTrigger rollback if any of the below persists for >10 minutes (or is severe immediately):\\n* p95 latency regression >= 10% (same route/model cohort)\\n* p99 latency regression >= 15%\\n* 5xx rate regression >= +0.25% absolute\\n* Any OOM burst (>= 3 OOMs within 15 minutes) on L40S pools\\n* Scheduler health degradation:\\n  * sustained queue depth above alert threshold (see below)\\n  * request drop/backpressure events above baseline by 2x\\n\\nh1. Stage 2\\u20134 \\u2014 Expansion rollout (10% \\u2192 25% \\u2192 50%+ \\u2192 100%)\\nGoal: expand while preserving the ability to correlate regressions with the rollout.\\n\\nh2. General rules\\n* Expand one dimension at a time:\\n  * either increase traffic share in one region, or add one new region at same share.\\n* Hold each stage for at least:\\n  * 2 hours during business hours, or\\n  * 1 peak window for that region (recommended)\\n* Record a short change note in the release channel including:\\n  * profile pack version\\n  * pools/regions affected\\n  * any notable metric shifts\\n\\nh2. Expansion checklist (repeat at each stage)\\n1) Confirm selected_profile distribution matches plan.\\n2) Compare latency/throughput segmented by:\\n   * region\\n   * pool\\n   * model family\\n   * streaming vs non-streaming\\n3) Watch for cohort-specific regressions (often only long-context or high-concurrency cohorts).\\n4) Confirm autoscaling and backpressure behavior is unchanged or improved.\\n\\nh1. Alert thresholds (rollout-time)\\nThese are rollout-time thresholds used to decide whether to pause/rollback. They are *not* contractual SLOs.\\n\\nh2. Latency thresholds (per route/model cohort)\\n* Warning:\\n  * p95 +7% vs trailing 7-day baseline (same time-of-day)\\n  * p99 +10%\\n* Critical / rollback consideration:\\n  * p95 +10% sustained 10 minutes\\n  * p99 +15% sustained 10 minutes\\n\\nh2. Error thresholds\\n* Warning:\\n  * 5xx +0.15% absolute vs baseline\\n  * retry rate +0.2% absolute\\n* Critical:\\n  * 5xx +0.25% absolute sustained 10 minutes\\n  * specific error signatures: CUDA OOM, illegal memory access, NCCL errors\\n\\nh2. Memory/OOM thresholds\\n* H100:\\n  * Critical: >= 2 OOMs in 30 minutes in same pool\\n* L40S:\\n  * Critical: >= 3 OOMs in 15 minutes (lower headroom; treat as urgent)\\n* Any GPU:\\n  * Critical: allocator failures or fragmentation warnings correlated with profile enablement\\n\\nh2. Scheduler/queueing thresholds\\n* Warning:\\n  * queue depth p95 +25% vs baseline\\n  * backpressure events 1.5x baseline\\n* Critical:\\n  * drop rate > 0 (if system previously configured to never drop)\\n  * sustained queue depth p95 +50% for 10 minutes\\n\\nh1. Rollback and mitigation\\nh2. Rollback hierarchy (prefer least disruptive)\\n1) *Disable profiles for the affected pool/region* (feature toggle)\\n2) *Pin to previous profile pack version* for the affected pool/region\\n3) *Revert runtime release* (only if issue is in loader/selection logic)\\n\\nh2. Rollback targets\\n* Per pool/region rollback (preferred)\\n* Per GPU SKU rollback if issue is SKU-specific (e.g., L40S memory guardrails)\\n* Per deployment-mode rollback (e.g., Private customers pinned differently)\\n\\nh2. Rollback procedure (pool/region)\\n1) Declare rollout paused in the release channel and tag SRE oncall.\\n2) Disable profiles in the affected pool/region.\\n3) Confirm within 10\\u201315 minutes:\\n   * selected_profile metric drops to \\u201cnone/default\\u201d (or expected fallback)\\n   * latency/error metrics return toward baseline\\n4) If not recovering, pin to last-known-good runtime config (pre-profile defaults) and escalate to Runtime oncall.\\n\\nh2. Version rollback procedure (profile pack)\\n1) Update pool configuration to pin *profile_pack_version = last_known_good*.\\n2) Restart or roll nodes according to pool policy.\\n3) Verify at startup:\\n   * profile_pack_version matches pinned\\n   * compatibility_result == ok\\n\\nh2. Mitigations short of rollback\\nUse only when rollback is costly and regression is localized.\\n* Reduce max batch size / tighten queue limits (protect tail latency)\\n* Reduce KV cache budget / enable stricter KV cache guardrails (prevent OOM)\\n* Disable specific kernel-selection toggles (if the regression signature matches known issue)\\n* Adjust prefill/decode fairness knobs (if p95 tail regresses under streaming/tool-calling mixes)\\n\\nh1. Incident response playbook (profile-related regression)\\nUse this when *stop criteria* is met or customer impact is reported.\\n\\nh2. Step 1 \\u2014 Identify blast radius (5\\u201310 minutes)\\n1) Confirm whether issue correlates with:\\n   * profile enablement time\\n   * specific pool/region\\n   * specific GPU SKU\\n   * specific model family or context-length cohort\\n2) Check selected_profile / override_source metrics for anomalies:\\n   * unknown SKU\\n   * unexpected override source\\n   * profile flapping after restarts\\n\\nh2. Step 2 \\u2014 Stabilize service (10\\u201320 minutes)\\n1) If error rate or OOMs are elevated: *disable profiles* in affected pool immediately.\\n2) If tail latency is elevated but errors stable:\\n   * prefer disabling profiles first\\n   * alternatively reduce batching/queue knobs (if disabling profiles is not possible due to policy)\\n3) Confirm stabilization on dashboards.\\n\\nh2. Step 3 \\u2014 Collect evidence (while stabilization occurs)\\nCollect and attach to incident ticket:\\n* pool/region list, SKU\\n* runtime version + profile pack version\\n* selected_profile distribution snapshot\\n* top error signatures and counts\\n* representative request cohorts (seq len bucket, streaming on/off)\\n* runtime startup logs (compatibility + selection)\\n\\nh2. Step 4 \\u2014 Triage root cause (30\\u201390 minutes)\\nCommon root causes:\\n* *Profile selection mismatch*: SKU string variant not normalized; wrong profile applied.\\n* *Tail-latency regression*: prefill/decode fairness or queue limits too aggressive for traffic mix.\\n* *OOM/regression on L40S*: KV cache budget too large; fragmentation; long-context cohorts.\\n* *B200 experimental instability*: driver/CUDA mismatch; kernels not mature; must remain gated.\\n\\nh2. Step 5 \\u2014 Follow-up actions\\n* File/associate issue with:\\n  * profile pack version\\n  * runtime version\\n  * dashboards\\n  * mitigation applied\\n* Add/adjust perf-canary gate if regression was not caught.\\n* Update known-issues page with signature + mitigation.\\n\\nh1. Private and Dedicated deployment notes\\nh2. Dedicated pools\\n* Prefer pool-level enablement with clear rollback path.\\n* Ensure customer-facing SLAs are not described as \\u201cguaranteed improvements\\u201d; use \\u201cexpected behavior\\u201d.\\n\\nh2. Private deployments\\n* Customers may pin profile versions and override select knobs via Helm values.\\n* Supportability requirement: customer overrides must remain within documented guardrails.\\n* When troubleshooting:\\n  * request the output of \\u201cdump effective runtime config\\u201d\\n  * verify the override order and which layer introduced the change\\n\\nh1. B200-specific guardrails\\n* B200 profile is *experimental* until the maturity criteria is met.\\n* Must be behind an explicit feature flag.\\n* Only enable in approved pools/regions with Infra + SRE sign-off.\\n* Default fallback must be defined (e.g., \\u201cno profile / safe defaults\\u201d) when compatibility check fails.\\n\\nMaturity criteria (minimum):\\n* 2 consecutive weeks of canary with no critical incidents\\n* workload matrix green for representative models and seq length buckets\\n* stable driver/CUDA baseline documented\\n\\nh1. Post-rollout checklist\\nWithin 2 business days of full enablement:\\n1) Publish a short summary:\\n   * perf deltas (latency/throughput) per SKU\\n   * any trade-offs observed\\n   * final pinned versions\\n2) Confirm dashboards are updated to segment by selected_profile.\\n3) Ensure oncall playbook links are current.\\n4) Update the \\u201cexpected behavior\\u201d docs and known issues list.\\n\\nh1. Appendix A \\u2014 Quick decision tree\\n* Elevated 5xx or CUDA errors? \\u2192 Disable profiles in affected pool immediately.\\n* OOM burst on L40S? \\u2192 Disable profiles or tighten KV cache budget; treat as urgent.\\n* Tail latency up (p95/p99) with stable errors? \\u2192 Disable profiles first; if not possible, reduce batching / adjust fairness.\\n* Only one region affected? \\u2192 Roll back only that region/pool; keep others unchanged.\\n* Only one SKU affected? \\u2192 Roll back SKU profile or pin to prior pack version.\\n\\nh1. Appendix B \\u2014 Standard change note template\\nUse in #eng-releases and #eng-runtime (or equivalent):\\n\\n*Change:* Enable Hardware Profiles Pack\\n*Runtime version:* <runtime-x.y.z>\\n*Profile pack version:* <profiles-a.b.c>\\n*Scope:* <region/pools>, <SKU>\\n*Stage:* Canary / 25% / 100%\\n*Dashboards:* <links>\\n*Owner:* <name>\\n*Rollback:* Disable profiles in <pool> / pin to <previous version>\\n\\nh1. Appendix C \\u2014 Contact checklist\\nWhen paging or escalating, include:\\n* pool/region + SKU\\n* runtime + profile pack versions\\n* regression type (latency / throughput / errors / OOM)\\n* time window + graphs\\n* mitigation already attempted\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c2289fb6eb774ab581564cd191db1fb6\"\n}",
